document: How CI executes the M5 conformance campaign
note: This contract is the canonical execution description beside the shard/merge scripts. The dedicated workflow owns fail-closed pull-request routing, deterministic PostgreSQL 15/18 target sharding, canonical report merge, and lightweight required-context emission.
identity_note: workflow_git_blob, script_git_blob, and merge_script_git_blob are the fail-closed authority. Each is the exact git hash-object identity of executable CI machinery; any byte-level drift makes retained evidence stale and must be deliberately re-proved. Literal fields remain readable diagnostics rather than the trust boundary.
matrix_note: The two ends of the supported PostgreSQL 15-18 range. Each major owns two deterministic target shards and one canonical merged report.

database.image_digest_note: The workflow appends an immutable Docker Hub multi-arch digest selected only from the checked-in PostgreSQL 15/18 matrix; 15 is 926f8799aef36e00001cfe15fba7abbd37d3c5224ea57e4c858e4bb670f10561 and 18 is 4ef4dbc939d61acea57712655ddb4b4ab27419c913f94cca0cd57cb3ea3c2280. Unsupported matrix values resolve to an invalid digest and fail before execution.

profile_note: Debug, like every M5 campaign except performance, whose denominator requires release for figures comparable to release planning. The conformance campaign gates correctness — every accepted row's scenarios ran and passed, on both PostgreSQL majors — not a duration, so nothing here depends on the profile.
features: the execution envelope's selected targets are built and run with --all-features by cargo xtask conformance's own target invocations

target_selection.source: the (package, target) pairs the accepted-scope document's scenario assignments name
target_selection.note: The 133 assigned scenarios name 30 unique targets. The producer derives those 30 exactly, partitions them one-to-one across two deterministic shards per PostgreSQL major, runs every selected target in full, then reconciles all 133 scenarios only after canonical merge.
target_selection.selected_targets_run_in_full_note: A selected target is not filtered down to only the scenarios that put it in the envelope: every test in that target binary runs, and the target's own exit status gates the campaign. A test inside a selected target that the accepted scope never named still runs and can still fail the campaign; only a target outside the envelope entirely is excluded.

pass_condition.assigned_scenarios_must_report_ok_note: Every one of the 133 assignments must resolve to a test that ran and reported ok. ignored, FAILED, or never having run is a violation.
pass_condition.selected_target_exit_must_succeed_note: Every one of the 30 selected targets must exit successfully as a process, independent of the scenario-level check above. This is the source of the 'selected targets run in full' behavior: a non-assigned test failing inside a selected target fails this condition even though no assigned scenario failed.
pass_condition.workspace_documentation_tests_must_pass_: A third, separate obligation: cargo test --workspace --all-features --doc. Shard zero owns it exactly once per PostgreSQL major; canonical merge rejects missing or duplicated documentation proof.

artifact_retention: 30 days, on success and on failure alike, because what a failed conformance campaign is mostly worth reading for is which accepted row, or which selected target, it lost
timeout_note: Each shard keeps the prior 55-minute safety ceiling; the canonical merge job has a separate 15-minute ceiling. The optimization changes wall-clock topology, not the proof deadline semantics.

pr_routing.trusted_classifier: .github/scripts/pr-scope.py from the exact pull request base SHA
pr_routing.failure_mode: trusted checkout, API, metadata, classifier, parser, output, or route-job ambiguity requires deep execution
pr_routing.no_direct_mode: emit the PostgreSQL 15/18 required contexts without provisioning PostgreSQL services

sharding.partition: round-robin over the canonical sorted (package, target) execution envelope
